# FilmDevMate

> An app for developing black and white film at home. You pick a film and a
> developer, and the app gives you the times, temperature and dilution for that
> combination, then runs the process as a timer that moves between steps on its
> own.

FilmDevMate is free, supported by ads, and available for iOS and Android.
It is made by an independent developer, not a film manufacturer.

## What it does

- **Recipes.** Development times for combinations of film and developer,
  covering 135, 120 and 4x5. Each recipe carries its dilution, ISO,
  temperature and the time for each format.
- **Timer.** Loads a recipe as a sequence of steps (develop, stop, fix, wash),
  advances between them automatically and notifies at each step boundary.
  Steps can be edited. On iOS the remaining time appears on the Lock Screen
  and in the Dynamic Island.
- **Dilution mixer.** Converts a ratio and a target volume into the amounts to
  pour. For example, 1+50 at 650ml is 12.7ml of stock and 637.3ml of water.
  Includes a unit converter for recipes written in imperial units.
- **Development log.** Records what was actually done for each roll so the
  same result can be repeated.
- **Development map.** Each film and developer combination is a tile that is
  claimed by developing it, shared with other users who have developed it more.

## What it is not

- Not a scanner or an editor. It does not process images.
- Not a source of chemistry. It does not sell or supply developer.
- Recipe times come from the community and from published manufacturer data.
  They are a starting point, not a guarantee; results vary with agitation,
  water and the age of the developer.

## Reference pages

Written out in full, and usable without the app:

- How to calculate a developer dilution (1+50 is fifty-one parts, not fifty):
  https://yezji.github.io/filmdevmate-web/dilution/
- Developing at the wrong temperature (22C instead of 20C):
  https://yezji.github.io/filmdevmate-web/temperature/
- The order and timing of black and white development:
  https://yezji.github.io/filmdevmate-web/steps/

Korean and Japanese versions live under /ko/ and /ja/.
